Description: Measure of overall economic size used in cross country economic comparisons
Interpretation: Used to indicate national capacity and not individual welfare distribution

Description: Log scaled representation of economic size for cross country comparison
Interpretation: Emphasizes relative differences between very large and smaller economies

Description: Indicator of short term economic performance momentum and macroeconomic stability
Interpretation: Positive values support growth narratives while negative values signal stress or contraction

Description: Indicator of average economic development and material living standards
Interpretation: Commonly used to argue development gaps policy capacity and aid eligibility

Description: Measure of public debt burden and fiscal constraints in policy debates
Interpretation: Often cited to argue vulnerability financing limits or need for restructuring

Description: Measure of integration into global trade through imports and exports relative to GDP
Interpretation: Often cited in debates on globalization exposure and external vulnerability

Description: Indicator of labor market conditions and economic inclusion in development debates
Interpretation: Often cited to justify employment policy reforms or targeted economic assistance

Description: Sovereign state used as the unit of representation in MUN debate contexts
Interpretation: Used for identification filtering and comparison and not a numeric indicator

Description: Classification of political system and institutional structure in diplomatic contexts
Interpretation: Provides regime background and is not suitable for quantitative ranking

Description: Indicator of physical size and territorial scale relevant to geographic context
Interpretation: Used to contextualize population distribution resources and geographic constraints

Description: Indicator of population concentration settlement patterns and spatial pressure
Interpretation: Used to contextualize urbanization infrastructure strain and resource stress

Description: Indicator of fertility and population growth dynamics relevant to social policy
Interpretation: Higher values support arguments on youth share service demand and resource pressure

Description: Key health and child welfare indicator in humanitarian and development discussions
Interpretation: Higher values often justify healthcare investment or international support

Description: Indicator of digital access connectivity and information infrastructure readiness
Interpretation: Used to discuss digital divide service delivery and modernization capacity

Description: Measure of basic educational attainment and human capital capacity
Interpretation: Higher values strengthen claims of education access and implementation readiness

Description: Measure of population age structure relevant to long term social planning
Interpretation: Used to discuss aging pressures youth bulges and workforce dynamics

Description: Indicator of long term population growth potential and demographic transition stage
Interpretation: Higher values may raise concerns about schooling jobs and resource needs

Description: Indicator of total national contribution to global carbon emissions
Interpretation: Used to discuss aggregate impact mitigation expectations and global responsibility

Description: Log scaled representation of total emissions to compare large and small emitters
Interpretation: Highlights relative differences while reducing dominance of major emitters

Description: Measure of individual level emissions footprint and consumption linked impact
Interpretation: Used to argue responsibility fairness and per capita burden sharing

Description: Log scaled per capita emissions to compare proportional responsibility
Interpretation: Emphasizes differences without letting high outliers dominate comparisons

Description: Indicator of carbon efficiency in economic production and energy systems
Interpretation: Higher values suggest less sustainable pathways and higher mitigation difficulty

Description: Log scaled carbon intensity to compare efficiency across wide development levels
Interpretation: Highlights relative efficiency gaps across economies with different structures
